title: Experiment with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 for Agentic Coding | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Alibaba's preview Qwen4-architecture model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B-parameter MoE with a hybrid Gated DeltaNet/sparse-attention design targeting million-token agentic coding workloads, gets immediate Day-0 NVIDIA support across inference engines and hits over 16K tokens/sec/GPU on GB300 NVL72 — evidence that leading Chinese open-weight labs and NVIDIA's newest Blackwell Ultra rack-scale platform remain tightly co-optimized despite geopolitical friction over chip exports.

insights.claim: NVIDIA provided best-effort Day-0 functional support for Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next across SGLang, vLLM, and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM, plus validation on GB300 NVL72 and post-training recipes via NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel and NeMo RL, immediately upon Alibaba's release of the model weights.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Same-day optimization support for a leading Chinese lab's frontier open-weight model shows NVIDIA continuing to treat Alibaba/Qwen as a top-tier ecosystem partner despite US-China chip export tensions — a signal that open-weight Chinese models remain commercially important demand drivers for NVIDIA's newest hardware (GB300/Blackwell Ultra) among global developers who can access it.
insights.quote: NVIDIA provides best-effort Day 0 functional support through SGLang, vLLM, and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM, validation across NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 for inference, and post-training recipes from NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel and NVIDIA NeMo RL.

insights.claim: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as an explicit preview of its upcoming Qwen4 architecture, ahead of a full Qwen4 launch, to let developers experiment and evaluate early.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: This flags Qwen4 as a near-term open-weight model release to watch; the architectural bets validated here (hybrid linear-attention + sparse retrieval) likely carry forward into Qwen4 and signal where competitive pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic/Google model economics is heading from Chinese open-weight labs.
insights.quote: Alibaba released the model weights for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as a preview of the upcoming Qwen4 architecture for developers to experiment with and evaluate.

insights.claim: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 125B total parameters plus an additional 51B N-gram embedding parameters, but activates only 6B parameters per token, and has a native 262,144-token context window extensible to 1M tokens using YaRN.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: A 6B-active/125B-total sparse MoE ratio (roughly 5% activation) shows continued industry momentum toward extreme sparsity to cut inference compute cost per token while preserving capacity — a key lever in the ongoing decline of inference cost curves across the industry.
insights.quote: It's a multimodal mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with a 125B-parameter main model supplemented by an additional 51B N-gram embeddings, with 6B parameters activated per token.

insights.claim: The model uses a hybrid architecture where three of every four layers use Gated DeltaNet (GDN) to continuously compress historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, eliminating KV-cache growth as sequences lengthen, while the remaining one-in-four layer uses Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) for precise full-context retrieval.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: This 3:1 linear-attention-to-sparse-attention ratio is a concrete engineering pattern for solving the KV-cache memory wall at million-token context — investors tracking inference infrastructure costs should note that architectural innovation (not just more HBM) is now a primary lever for cutting long-context serving costs.
insights.quote: Three out of every four layers use GDN to continuously compress historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, eliminating KV cache growth as sequences lengthen. The remaining layer uses QSA for precise retrieval across the full context.

insights.claim: Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) aggregates sequences into micro-blocks and estimates importance at the block level rather than the token level (unlike prior sparse-attention indexers), which Alibaba's benchmarks show delivers up to 7.6x prefill and 4.9x decoding speedups versus full attention.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Block-level sparse attention avoiding the growing overhead of token-level indexers is a scalability fix specifically for very long contexts; a claimed 7.6x prefill speedup is a large efficiency gain that, if it holds outside Alibaba's own benchmarks, materially lowers the cost of agentic/tool-heavy workloads that reprocess large contexts repeatedly.
insights.quote: its attention kernel delivered speedups of up to 7.6x during prefill and 4.9x during decoding.

insights.claim: In a cache-heavy online-serving test at 1M-token context with a 90% prefix-cache hit rate, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieved 8.6x the prefill throughput of Alibaba's prior model Qwen3.7-Plus.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: An 8.6x prefill throughput gain generation-over-generation at long context is a large jump in serving economics for agentic coding and document-processing use cases with high context reuse, suggesting Alibaba's model line is optimizing specifically for repeat-context agentic workloads rather than one-shot chat.
insights.quote: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieved 8.6x the prefill throughput of Qwen3.7-Plus.

themes.theme: GB300 NVL72 rack-scale performance and product-tier strategy

insights.claim: GB300 NVL72 integrates 72 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs into a single rack-scale NVLink domain delivering 130 TB/s of all-to-all bandwidth, which the article credits with eliminating bottlenecks that appear when MoE expert traffic must cross traditional off-the-shelf networks.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: This reinforces that NVIDIA's rack-scale NVLink domain, not just individual GPU FLOPs, is the differentiator for serving large sparse MoE models efficiently — a durable structural advantage over competitors lacking comparable scale-up interconnect at 130 TB/s.
insights.quote: Its large, 72-GPU NVIDIA NVLink domain enables efficient all-to-all communication at 130 TB/s, eliminating bottlenecks that appear when expert traffic must cross traditional off-the-shelf networks.
insights.locator: section 'Running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72'

insights.claim: Running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on GB300 NVL72 delivers over 16,000 tokens per second per GPU and over 200 tokens per second per user.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: These are concrete unit-economics figures (throughput per GPU and per user) investors can use as a benchmark data point for GB300-generation inference cost-per-token and for gauging whether newly announced open-weight models can hit interactive latency thresholds needed for real-time agentic coding products.
insights.quote: Running on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 delivers over 16K tokens per second per GPU and over 200 tokens per second per user, enabling developers to experiment with agentic coding applications at high throughput and low latency.
insights.locator: section 'Running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72'

insights.claim: Beyond rack-scale GB300 NVL72, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next also runs on NVIDIA's smaller local hardware tiers: DGX Station, DGX Spark clusters, and workstations with four NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition GPUs, letting developers prototype locally and scale the identical model to rack-scale production without re-architecting.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: This full-tier product strategy (workstation to rack) is how NVIDIA captures developer mindshare early (cheap local hardware) and converts it into production rack-scale hardware sales later, reinforcing the CUDA-style funnel from prototyping to deployment entirely within NVIDIA's hardware line.
insights.locator: section 'Running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72'

insights.claim: NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel offers Day-0 Hugging Face checkpoint support, letting developers fine-tune Qwen3.8-Flash-Next directly on existing checkpoints without model conversion, using either full supervised fine-tuning or memory-efficient LoRA, with a further option to run reinforcement learning via NeMo RL recipes.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Zero-conversion Day-0 fine-tuning support lowers the switching cost for enterprises adopting new open-weight models on NVIDIA infrastructure, which helps NVIDIA capture post-training compute spend regardless of which foundation-model lab wins mindshare.
insights.quote: Train directly on existing checkpoints without model conversion, with support for full SFT or memory-efficient LoRA fine-tuning.
insights.locator: section 'Post-train Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and serve it with your preferred inference engine'

insights.claim: NVIDIA supports the model across multiple independent inference engines (SGLang, vLLM, and TokenSpeed) rather than pushing developers toward a single proprietary serving stack.
insights.speaker: Rajath Narasimha
insights.so_what: Remaining inference-engine-agnostic maximizes the odds that any given deployment still runs on NVIDIA silicon underneath, regardless of which serving framework a developer prefers — a strategy of owning the hardware layer while staying neutral on software choice.
insights.quote: SGLang, vLLM, and TokenSpeed provide open-source inference recipes for developers requiring greater control over performance on the NVIDIA-accelerated platform.
insights.locator: section 'Post-train Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and serve it with your preferred inference engine'
